messages:
alex.k: Hey @sara-peopleops — need to add my dad to benefits (he's 62, lives in EU). I'm traveling and can't get a lot of notarized docs before the open enrollment cutoff on May 1. SSN not available (he has an ITIN). Can we still add him? What specific docs do you need and how does payroll proration work? Thanks!

sara-peopleops: Hi @alex.k — short answer: maybe. We can add international dependents but we need acceptable proof. Typically we need one government ID (passport), plus proof of relationship/financial dependency (bank transfers, shared household docs, or a signed declaration). For international docs we accept translations with an apostille or certified translator. If you can't get notarization before May 1, upload what you have and a receipt showing you requested translations/notarization — that can be accepted temporarily.

alex.k: The dependency is financial support — I've been sending monthly transfers since Jan 15. I don't have guardianship or anything like that. Will bank transfer history + a municipal residency certificate work? Also: is this considered a QLE?

sara-peopleops: That sounds like a valid QLE if the qualifying event is the date you started providing primary financial support or a change in dependent status. We'll need the event date to process as a QLE. Bank transfer history + residency cert is a good start. For payroll: we can accept ITIN instead of SSN, but payroll needs the tax identifier on file. Premiums are usually prorated from the effective date. If you request retroactive coverage we'll need stronger docs and approval (see below). Upload via the People Ops portal (Benefits > Add dependent > QLE). Link: https://benefits.redwood.com/portal (paste into browser).

ben-payroll: looping in payroll — @ben-payroll here. We accept ITINs for benefits enrollment. For proration: premiums are charged pro-rata from the benefit effective date. Standard effective date for QLEs is the date of the event, but if that date is before the request and you want retro coverage, we need supporting docs and a review. Retro requests may be approved up to the start of the plan year in exceptional cases, but typically we can only backdate to the event date if docs show continuous dependency.

natalie-peopleops: A few practical notes: 1) If translations will take longer than 14 days, upload a scanned original + the translation request/receipt so we can provisionally accept. 2) You can redact bank account numbers (leave name, dates, and amounts visible). 3) For the portal upload choose "International dependent" checkbox so the reviewers see the country flag and routing.

alex.k: Great — thanks. I'll upload bank transfer CSV (redacted), passport scan, and the municipal residency PDF tonight. Quick question: if we upload an initial packet now and the final translated apostille comes later, will that delay the effective date?

ben-payroll: If the initial packet is sufficient to establish dependency and event date, we can set the effective date based on that. Translations/final apostille can be added to complete the record; they usually don't block an initial effective date unless the relationship is in question. If payroll needs the tax ID and it's pending, add the ITIN placeholder and a note.

hr-bot: Reminder: open enrollment window closes May 1 23:59 PT. QLE documentation for outside-window events should be submitted within 30 days of the event to avoid denial.

alex.k: Uploaded files in the portal (file name: alex_dad_docpacket_2149.zip). Included: passport_scan.pdf, bank_transfers_redacted.csv, residency_cert.pdf, translation_receipt.pdf. Notarized translation pending — receipt included.

sara-peopleops: Got the upload, thanks. We'll start review and ping if anything missing. Expect initial confirmation within 7 business days (by May 10). If you need retroactive premium adjustment request, indicate "Retro request" in the upload notes and provide a short timeline of support since Jan.

alex.k: Perfect — thanks everyone! :thumbsup:
